$comment: Every operation id in the backend's operationPolicy. scope is the broadest scope it may be offered at; subject, required, is true when the operation is about the member the request's subject names and false when it is about the target itself (the request's subject is then empty); confirm is whether the backend requires it; effect is read (served through Syndra's one read path: never dispatched, logged or confirmed), account, credential or physical; result names the schema the add-on answers under result, the one key every read answers under (health.get declares its own and is shown raw). secret_result marks an operation whose reply carries a secret: the add-on records it redacted, and a replay and GET /calls answer recorded without it; none does yet. A physical operation is confirmed, needs feature calls, and is never resent; a param's format target_id is an id typed or scanned on the target (a UI hint; the add-on answers UNKNOWN_RESOURCE for one that names nothing).

account.adopt.meaning: Bind an existing unbound target account to the subject.

account.purge.meaning: Remove a disabled account from the target, with an elevated credential.

account.release.meaning: Forget the binding without touching the account.

activity.get.meaning: What the subject did on the target, read live.

health.get.meaning: The target's own health, read live.

holdings.list.meaning: What the subject holds on the target, read live.

item.checkout.meaning: The member takes an item: the add-on records a loan of item_id to the subject.

password.rotate.meaning: Replace the subject's password with a generated one the member never sees.

password.set.meaning: The member sets their own password.

storage.status.meaning: Whether the member can use the storage and how much room is left, read live.
